title: JANUS Engine — TOPA + Spider magnetic Axle drive / cogging / electropermanent comparison
mission: test whether timed cancellation of braking permanent-magnet sectors can improve Axle motion
compare passive alternating magnets, active torque-ripple compensation, electropermanent/variable-flux switching, hybrid excitation, and coreless axial-flux PM starter-generator topologies
select the topology that best fits JANUS low-starting-torque, bidirectional starter/generator and low-parasitic requirements

literature_findings.finding: Coreless and slotless AFPM topologies eliminate slot-effect cogging torque and are repeatedly used where low starting torque matters. Reviews also note removal of iron/hysteresis losses, while tradeoffs include larger magnetic air-gap/leakage flux, structural stiffness and higher PM/copper burden.
references: IET Electric Power Applications 2022 systematic review, DOI 10.1049/elp2.12218

literature_findings.finding: Position-synchronous harmonic-current injection and adaptive learning controllers can generate an opposing electromagnetic torque to reduce periodic torque ripple. This is a control tool, not a net-energy source; copper/core/inverter losses must be charged.

Low-coercivity magnets can have their magnetization state changed by short current pulses and then retain the new state without continuous field current. This is attractive for infrequent operating-mode changes, but repeated re/de-magnetization has finite pulse energy and hysteretic/copper losses.
references: CES Transactions on Electrical Machines and Systems 2018, DOI 10.23919/TEMS.2018.8326450
Electrical Engineering / VFMM pulse-trajectory study 2023: tested +30 A and -25 A pulses; measured re/de-magnetization operation losses in the tens of joules on that prototype
literature_findings.boundary: The reported pulse energies are machine-specific and are not directly scalable to JANUS; they nevertheless show that per-sector magnetic-state reversal is not intrinsically free or lossless.

literature_findings.finding: Adding controlled field excitation to PM machines gives useful flux enhancement/weakening and can improve operating range, but adds copper, thermal and control complexity.

physics_result_for_timed_negative_torque.model: For a conservative PM interaction with torque tau_PM(theta), the work over a complete mechanical cycle is integral(tau_PM dtheta)=0 when magnetic state and geometry return to the same state.
physics_result_for_timed_negative_torque.half_cycle_argument: If the positive half-cycle is left passive but an active coil cancels the negative half-cycle, the coil must supply the mechanical work needed to restore the magnetic-field configuration. In an ideal lossless actuator the electrical/mechanical work supplied by the coil equals the apparent positive PM work harvested over the cycle; with real losses the required electrical energy is greater.
physics_result_for_timed_negative_torque.conclusion: Timed cancellation can smooth torque and reduce a troublesome cogging barrier, but it cannot turn a passive PM pattern into a net source. It is equivalent to an actively commutated motor/actuator function and should be judged by total electrical-to-mechanical efficiency.

architecture_screen.reason: Produces magnetic wells/cogging and zero ideal net work per closed cycle.
Valid for ripple/cogging cancellation and precise speed control, but the cancelling current supplies the missing work and adds copper/inverter loss.

Nonvolatile switching is attractive, but repeated magnetization-state pulses every pole passage are poorly matched to the JANUS single-digit/low-tens-of-watts parasitic budget. Reserve for infrequent mode/latch/valve states.
Strong flux-control capability but more magnetic iron, field winding, heat and control complexity than needed for the first Axle demonstrator.

Best fit for low starting torque and bidirectional operation: slot-effect cogging is eliminated, the same unit can motor the Axle from the battery during startup and generate/regenerate when the Axle has real mechanical input.

selected_architecture.name: JANUS_CORELESS_AFPM_AXLE_STARTER_GENERATOR
functions: small active torque-ripple compensation only if measured necessary
regenerative generation when real mechanical surplus exists
selected_architecture.mechanical_integration_preference: Prefer the electromagnetic machine on a dry-side Axle extension or across a non-ferromagnetic low-eddy-current barrier so magnets, windings and inverter electronics are isolated from the wet POMS/calcium chemistry loop.
selected_architecture.magnet_layout: Start with a conventional low-cogging PM array; Halbach or segmented/skewed magnets are optimization branches only after baseline FEM/bench data.
selected_architecture.control: Rotor position sensing plus three-phase inverter/FOC or equivalent synchronous commutation. Do not implement per-sector electropermanent demagnetization in the baseline.

hard_invariants: REGENERATION_IS_COUNTED_ONLY_WHEN A REAL MECHANICAL SOURCE DRIVES THE AXLE
